evidence.note: Titles on s-1, s-3, s-4, s-5 and s-7 state specific, sourced findings as single sentences with no trailing full stop, matching the profile's approved title rule.
'The drop is a diversion problem, not a fleet or staffing one' is an 'X, not Y' antithesis the profile bans in body copy.

'On-time departures fell from 86% to 81% in Q3, and retiming the diverted routes is the Q4 test' is an 'X, and Y' two-clause title with a framing closer ('the Q4 test'), a pattern the profile rejected as AI-sounding.
Title joins two findings with ', and' ('closed in three phases from 7 July, and routes 12 and 14 ran the diversion without retiming'), the same rejected X-and-Y construction.
'Retime routes 12 and 14 Cross-town for the diversion in Q4' is an imperative heading; the profile converts imperatives to findings.
'...is the Q4 test, checked at the end of January' repeats the 'test' framing rather than stating a finding.
Insight explains cause to consequence plainly ('A fleet or staffing shortfall would cut recovery time on every route, so the Q3 drop points to the diversion'), matching approved overlays.
Driver quote is verbatim with a neutral label and cite, no editorialising, as the narration-tile rule requires.
Three specific, grounded open questions (running time at the school run, what January result would separate the readings, lost mileage beside the target), matching the discussion-prompt rule.
Byline reads 'Orrin Valley Transit service planning, November 2026' rather than '<presenter name>, <Month year>'; minor.

rationale: Most copy follows the profile: finding titles, plain cause-to-consequence insights, verbatim quotes and grounded prompts. But there are several lapses the presenter has explicitly rejected before: an 'X, not Y' antithesis on s-2, two 'X, and Y' titles with a framing closer (s-2, s-6), an imperative tile heading, and the repeated 'Q4 test' framing. That fits level 3 better than level 4's 'one or two minor lapses'.
